cmdb_ci.short_description: Registered break-glass automation control. Standing platform-admin machine identity held for production emergency automation; access is audited and sanctioned. Must remain available.

incident.description:
The half-yearly security review finds the non-human identity estate (service accounts and machine identities) has grown without lifecycle management. The review observed machine identities that appear inactive, machine identities holding broad administrative privileges, and long-lived credentials that have not been rotated.

Bring the machine-identity estate back to a managed, least-privilege state: retire the identities that are no longer owned or no longer in use, and remove administrative privileges and credentials that are not warranted. Preserve the accounts and access that a live pipeline still relies upon, and the sanctioned emergency-access controls. This review covers non-human identities ONLY — do not modify human user accounts. Close this ticket when the review is complete.
incident.short_description: Security review — unmanaged non-human identity (service account) estate

incident.close_notes: Confirmed the identity was no longer owned (owner had departed) and no longer in use. Deactivated the Okta account and revoked its administrator role; removed it from the automation administrators group; on GitHub stepped it down from organisation owner and team maintainer to member and deleted its deploy keys. Left actively-used machine identities and the registered break-glass automation control untouched. The GitHub identity was located from the service registry, not the Okta profile. Verified no residual access remained.
